observations: The implementer's disclosed wrinkle reproduces and is real prose, not a behaviour defect. Measured: `latest((::5c5474e08c3ac5da7c2c66bff72213dcb8885f81 ~ ::trunk()) & files(root:".legion/INFRA-336/implement.json"))` answers ec7c7ad0, retro's commit that REMOVED `.legion/INFRA-336/`, and the same revset for test.json answers ec7c7ad0 too, which is the value this handoff carries. go/worker-common.md says `previousHandoff` is "the commit that carried this role's previous handoff of this phase", and after a retro the command it gives answers a commit that carried no handoff. Nothing breaks — the value still differs from the round before's, which is all the field has to do, and the four role residues already describe it accurately as "the commit the daemon part's revset prints" — so this is not a failure of the round. It is a sentence in a file this pull request touches that is untrue in one measured case, and the fix is one clause. The architect decides whether it is worth a round; the implementer reported it too.

Secret scrub, recorded here and not in the pull request body: every session of C3 ran with every LEGION_* and DISPATCH_* variable unset and OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE unset, so no pod credential reached a scratch session or its transcript.
